content:
incident-bot: Pager: dedicated-router error-rate spike -> 503s and apparent traffic blackholing (alert: ROUTER_HIGH_5XX)

maya (oncall): I'm paged, investigating now. seeing router 503 spikes across two dedicated pools in us-west1.

sam (infra): @maya are the autoscalers healthy? any recent config pushes to router routing-policy?

maya (oncall): checking autoscale logs. initial glance shows scale decisions dropping desired nodes for pool-dedicated-42 around the same minute traffic spiked.

ellie (runtime): hmm that pool serves model-variant:xq-3b-q8 and variant fallback to xq-3b-fp16 is configured. could it be routing to an incompatible variant?

maya (oncall): looking at router logs, there's a flood of route decisions to model-variant "xq-3b-fp16-mig" which we don't have nodes for in that pool (we only have q8 quantized images).

sam (infra): that sounds like a policy misconfig. I see a config change 2 hours ago from deploy-bot: `apply routing-policy --name canary-variant-fallback --pool selector=dedicated-42 --fallback variant=xq-3b-fp16-mig`

maya (oncall): @deploy-bot can you show the PR/commit?

deploy-bot: deployment: PR #1427 merged by @ellie 2026-03-15 09:12UTC - added canary fallback policy for regional continuity.

ellie (runtime): that PR was intended to route to fp16 in cloud pools only; looks like the selector had an unintended pool selector that included dedicated-42. my bad.

maya (oncall): ok root cause candidate: fallback policy pointing traffic to variant not present in dedicated pool -> router routes queued to nonexistent capacity -> autoscaler sees no healthy backends and interprets as low utilization -> scales down -> blackhole loop.

tony (prod-sre): can we revert that routing-policy immediately? we should also pause autoscaling for the affected pool as quick mitigation.

sam (infra): I can pause autoscale for pool-dedicated-42. running: `rbacctl pause-autoscale --pool dedicated-42 --by oncall`

sam (infra): paused autoscale for dedicated-42.

maya (oncall): thanks. I'm going to roll back the canary fallback in router. command: `routerctl policy delete canary-variant-fallback --env prod --scope dedicated-42`

ellie (runtime): I'm running rollback now and will exclude dedicated pools in the updated policy.

ellie (runtime): rollback applied. Please verify routing decisions.

maya (oncall): watching router decisions. traffic is flowing back to xq-3b-q8. 503 rate dropping.

leo (support): checking customer impact: several high-volume customers on dedicated plans reported degraded SLA in last 12 minutes. forwarding list.

customer-success: FYI, CS alerted a large partner (AcmeApps) and wants a concise summary for postmortem.

maya (oncall): quick impact summary for CS: ~12 minutes of elevated 5xx for dedicated-42 customers in us-west1, estimated 2.4k failed requests, mitigated by policy rollback and autoscale pause.

tony (prod-sre): recommend we keep autoscale paused for 10m after traffic stabilizes to avoid re-triggering during the routing fix propagation.

sam (infra): agreed. re-evaluating health checks and autoscale signal sources. preliminary thought: our autoscaler uses backend healthy count + CPU util. When router routes to variant with no endpoints, backend healthy count drops -> autoscaler thinks demand dropped and scales in. We need a guard: if route failure rate spikes, do not scale in.

ellie (runtime): that guard would've prevented this. filing an RFC: add routing-failure signal into autoscaler decision matrix and a cooldown for scale-in on high route-error.

ops-runbooks: runbook note: for now mitigation playbook = 1) pause autoscale 2) rollback misrouted policy 3) confirm traffic flows to existing variants 4) unpause autoscale after 10m of stable 5xx baseline.

maya (oncall): Confirming metrics: error rate back to baseline after ~4 minutes post-rollback.

sam (infra): unpause autoscale in 10m if stable. scheduling unpause at +10m: command queued.

ellie (runtime): follow-up actions: 1) revert PR #1427 to patch selector, 2) add guard in autoscaler (RFC), 3) add e2e test for fallback policies including dedicated pools.

tony (prod-sre): I'll own the postmortem and severity. recommend Sev2 (customer impact, brief outage).

customer-success: Can you tag impacted customers and send CS a short blurb? we'll prepare notification.

leo (support): tagging customers: AcmeApps, BetaCorp, FastShip. sending incident notes.

maya (oncall): handing off to @tony for postmortem and continuity. I will remain available for follow-ups for 30m.

tony (prod-sre): taking over. +1 on actions. please include logs/links below in the postmortem draft.

maya (oncall): logs: `s3://redwood-logs/prod/router/1850123456/*.log` and autoscale events: `gs://infra-events/prod/autoscale/2026-03-15/dedicated-42.json`

ellie (runtime): I'll update the PR and add an explicit pool-exclude test before reapplying.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: ROUTER_HIGH_5XX -> downgraded to INFO after 30m of baseline. Runbook step 'postmortem' assigned to @tony.

tony (prod-sre): posting initial incident summary to /incidents channel and starting the postmortem doc.

maya (oncall): marking this thread resolved on my side. thanks team :thumbsup:

leo (support): CS confirmed customers received notice, will follow up with any escalations.

ops-runbooks: bookmarking runbook changes: add autoscaler guard, test policy e2e.

ellie (runtime): apologizing for the misselector; will be more careful with scope in future.

maya (oncall): good work. closing thread.
